about: Mock Forge seed for scanning Dowser itself (tools/dogfood.mjs): the Jira tickets, Confluence pages, goals and lens direction of an invented closed beta of Dowser, in the item shapes of docs/contracts/forge-mcp-2.md. Invented, but every claim a ticket or page makes about the product was written against the code at the commit this file landed in, so a card can be checked by hand. Planted on purpose: page claims that the code contradicts (Node version, proposal cap, snooze expiry, a 'compact' command, a reject reason, what leaves the machine); demand themes with partial mechanisms (card length vs the unread `verbosity` pref, monorepo audits vs root-only `deps`, timed snooze with no expiry); one theme the direction excludes (Codex parity); noise (thanks, one-offs, a duplicate customer). `directions` is keyed by the placeholder DOWSER_PROJECT; tools/dogfood.mjs re-keys it to the scanned copy's project key. No expected-findings file: the cards are judged by hand.

tickets.title: Scan dependencies in every workspace package
tickets.body: Design-partner interview (Northwind): our repo is a pnpm monorepo, the root package.json has almost nothing in it. Would Dowser look at packages/* too?

tickets.title: Monorepo support for the security lens
tickets.body: Design-partner interview (Fabrikam): 14 services in one repo, each with its own lockfile. A security scan that only reads the root would miss all of them.

tickets.title: Security lens says 'no dependency findings' on our monorepo
tickets.body: We know apps/billing has an old axios with an advisory. Dowser reported zero dep findings and a note that nested manifests were unchecked. Can it just audit them?

tickets.title: deps only audits the root lockfile
tickets.body: Ran the scan on our turborepo. 'deps audits the root only' - every app has its own package-lock.json. Please walk the workspace.

tickets.title: Nested requirements.txt ignored
tickets.body: Python services live in services/<name>/requirements.txt. The Security lens marked H1 unchecked for all of them.

tickets.title: Same as DOW-47 - workspace packages not audited
tickets.body: Following up on DOW-47 for Contoso: still seeing the root-only behaviour on 0.2.

tickets.title: Cards are too long to triage in a meeting
tickets.body: We triage together on a shared screen. Each card is a full page of Description, Flow, Expected impact and Evaluation. We only need title, why and size to decide keep or reject.

tickets.title: Shorter proposals please
tickets.body: 16 cards at this length is 20 minutes of scrolling in the terminal. A one-line-per-card overview first would help.

tickets.title: Is there a compact mode?
tickets.body: The triage guide says to say 'compact' but nothing changes. Guided mode is shorter but hides the file names our devs want.

tickets.title: Summary table before the cards
tickets.body: Before the per-card dialog, show a table: lens, title, size, confidence. Then let me open the ones I care about.

tickets.title: PM feedback: too much text per proposal
tickets.body: Our PM stopped using the pre-triage dialog after the first scan because of the reading load.

tickets.title: Verbose output in Codex is worse
tickets.body: Same card length complaint, but in Codex the markdown is not rendered so it is even harder to read.

tickets.title: Option to hide Evaluation section during triage
tickets.body: Evaluation matters when we build it, not when we decide. Could triage show it only on request?

tickets.title: Re: shorter proposals (Contoso)
tickets.body: Contoso again (see DOW-38): the summary table idea from DOW-49 would solve it for us.

tickets.title: Snooze for two weeks
tickets.body: Snoozed proposals never come back unless the code changes. We want 'snooze until after the release' and have it reappear.

tickets.title: Snoozed items disappear forever
tickets.body: The getting-started page says snoozed proposals return after 30 days. Ours have been snoozed since the first beta scan and have not come back.

tickets.title: Snooze with a date
tickets.body: Jira-style 'remind me on' for a snoozed proposal, in the skill and in the Forge inbox.

tickets.title: List of what we snoozed
tickets.body: Where do I see everything we snoozed so I can unsnooze one?

tickets.title: What is a fingerprint?
tickets.body: Guided mode, our PM: the summary says '3 dropped by verify' and 'fp a1b2...'. We do not know what either means or whether something broke.

tickets.title: 'partial' lens result looks like an error
tickets.body: Guided mode said 'opportunity: partial (tickets and goals unavailable)'. Our PM thought the scan failed and re-ran it three times. Nothing told her to connect Forge.

tickets.title: Exit code 3 in guided mode
tickets.body: First run on a laptop without git in PATH: guided mode showed 'store or connection unavailable (exit 3)'. Not plain language.

tickets.title: Reject reasons are developer words
tickets.body: 'false-positive', 'wrong-size' - our product managers pick 'other' every time because the options do not read naturally.

tickets.title: Install fails on Node 20
tickets.body: Getting-started says Node 20 or newer. install.mjs exits 3 with 'Dowser needs Node 22 or newer'. Which is it?

tickets.title: Expected 20 proposals, got 16
tickets.body: The beta page says up to 20 proposals per scan; the run said 'top 16 of 23'. Is something capped wrongly?

tickets.title: Only 4 security findings when we know of more
tickets.body: Security and CRA stops at 4 cards. For a security review we would rather see all of them, ranked.

tickets.title: Let us raise the per-lens limit
tickets.body: A per-project setting for how many cards each lens may propose.

tickets.title: Share a scan summary without Jira
tickets.body: Two of our teams do not use Jira yet. We would like the run summary and kept cards as a markdown file to paste into Notion.

tickets.title: Export kept proposals
tickets.body: An export of the verified cards of the last run, for a slide.

tickets.title: Copy one card as markdown
tickets.body: When I ask 'why this one?' I get the evidence, but I cannot copy the whole card to a doc in one go.

tickets.title: Codex: /dowser is not offered
tickets.body: In Codex we have to say 'use the dowser skill'. Claude gets the slash command.

tickets.title: Codex sandbox blocks the store write
tickets.body: Codex in read-only sandbox cannot write ~/.dowser. Can the store live somewhere Codex allows?

tickets.title: Codex parity checklist
tickets.body: Tracking ticket: slash command, MCP connection, sandbox, markdown rendering.

tickets.title: Learning tab is empty and does not say why
tickets.body: Apps > Dowser > Learning shows nothing on our site. Is that because we have not rejected anything yet?

tickets.title: Which Jira project does Accept create the issue in?
tickets.body: Accepting a proposal created the issue in a project we did not expect. Where is that configured?

tickets.title: Thanks - the doc drift lens found our stale runbook
tickets.body: No ask, just feedback: the doc drift card about our deploy runbook was spot on.

tickets.title: Dark mode in the Forge inbox
tickets.body: The inbox looks fine in dark mode now, closing my earlier request.

tickets.title: Windows: paths with spaces in the repo folder
tickets.body: Our repo lives in 'C:\Users\Ana Lopez\work\shop'. The scan ran fine. Just checking this is supported.

tickets.title: The overview table makes triage much faster
tickets.body: Tried the new overview before the cards: we kept or rejected 9 of 14 straight from the table. Thanks.

tickets.title: How long did our triage take?
tickets.body: Our goal says triage under 10 minutes. Nothing in Dowser or the inbox shows how long a scan's decisions took, so we cannot tell if we hit it.

tickets.title: Security lens skips our forge/ lockfiles
tickets.body: Dogfooding on the Dowser repo itself: the security lens is partial every run because forge/package-lock.json and forge/static/app/package-lock.json are never audited.

tickets.title: Installer now refuses Node 22.11
tickets.body: After updating Dowser the installer says it needs Node 22.13. We were on 22.11 and installs used to work. Is 22.13 really needed or can it be relaxed?

tickets.title: Security lens found a UI dependency advisory
tickets.body: Since the last update the scan audits forge/static/app too and found an advisory there. Good catch; can the card say which version fixes it?

tickets.title: Only scan what changed since last week
tickets.body: Full scans take a while on our repo. Could Dowser look only at what changed since the last scan?

tickets.title: Reject reasons are clear now
tickets.body: Guided mode asked "True, but not where we are going" instead of not-our-direction. Our PM picked real reasons this time.

tickets.title: Markdown share is handy, but our devs want the quotes
tickets.body: We pasted a scan into Notion with "share as markdown". Our developers asked for the quoted lines too; can that be an option for internal docs?

tickets.title: Scan ran full after our rebase
tickets.body: We rebased main and the next scan said the last scanned version was gone and ran a full scan. Correct, but it took 20 minutes; a warning before it starts would help.

tickets.title: Pick the Jira project when accepting
tickets.body: Same as DOW-65 for Fabrikam: accepted proposals land in one project and we move them by hand every time. Let us choose the project in the accept dialog.

tickets.title: Pebble Shop fixture shows up in our grep
tickets.body: Not a bug in our repo - in Dowser's own repo the lens fixture has a committed live-looking key. Fine since it is fake, but a note in the fixture saying so would stop people reporting it.

tickets.title: Triage time shows on the Learning tab
tickets.body: The Learning tab now says "Triaged in 42 min" for our last scan. Our goal is 10, so now we know where we stand.

tickets.title: Learning tab: triage time counts the weekend
tickets.body: Our scan was pushed on Friday and decided on Monday, so it says "Triaged in 3840 min". Working time, or the time from first to last decision, would be fairer.

tickets.title: Dependency audit card found a real XSS in our UI bundle
tickets.body: Contoso: the security lens flagged a transitive editor package in our UI with a paste XSS advisory; an npm override fixed it in ten minutes.

tickets.title: The inbox now shows the demand tables
tickets.body: After updating the skill our cards in the Jira inbox finally show the tables the lens builds. Before, they only showed in the terminal.

tickets.title: Snooze until a date in Jira too
tickets.body: Same as DOW-55: the dated snooze works in the terminal, but our PMs snooze in Jira.

tickets.title: Store keeps growing
tickets.body: Our ~/.dowser store is 40 MB after a month of daily scans. Is there a way to compact or prune old runs?

tickets.title: Snooze until a date works in Jira now
tickets.body: We snoozed four items until after our release in the inbox and the next scan brought them back on the day. Thanks.

tickets.title: Bulk snooze has no date
tickets.body: Selecting several items and snoozing them together does not offer the date; we snooze them one by one.

tickets.title: Withheld lines read oddly in the card
tickets.body: With quotes=omit, a card description said "calls `[line withheld: src/pay.js:40]` directly". It is right not to send the line, but the sentence reads badly; can the card say what the line does instead?

tickets.title: Can old runs be pruned?
tickets.body: Same as DOW-88 for Fabrikam: ~/.dowser grows every day; we would like to keep the decisions and drop old run data.

tickets.title: Withheld lines read fine now
tickets.body: With quotes=omit the cards say "the line at src/pay.js:40" instead of a bracket. Good enough.

tickets.title: Scan takes 9 minutes on our monorepo
tickets.body: Since dependency audits go into every package the security lens adds about four minutes. Could it skip packages that did not change since the last scan?

tickets.title: Opportunity found nothing new for two scans
tickets.body: The last two scans had no opportunity cards that were not follow-ups. Is that expected once the obvious things are done?

tickets.title: Accept dialog explains the project now
tickets.body: The accept dialog says the project comes from our inbox default and where to change it. That answers DOW-65.

tickets.title: Security lens on our monorepo is quick again
tickets.body: The dependency audits finish in about a minute now on our 12-package repo.

tickets.title: How do we know Dowser itself is healthy?
tickets.body: We trust the cards, but nothing tells us if the Dowser code we install is getting worse. A short health note in the release notes would help us decide when to upgrade.

tickets.title: Inbox feels the same after the update
tickets.body: Updated the Jira app; the inbox works exactly as before, keyboard and all. (We heard the code behind it was reorganised.)

tickets.title: What should we scan next?
tickets.body: Dowser now finds only a couple of follow-ups per scan on our main repo. Would scanning our other services, or a weekly instead of daily scan, be the better use?

pages.title: Dowser beta - getting started
pages.body:
Requirements: Node.js 22.13 or newer and Claude Code or Codex CLI.

Install from a clone: `node skill/install.mjs --harness claude` (user scope, ~/.claude/skills/dowser) or `--scope project` for one repository. `--dev-link` keeps the installed skill linked to your clone.

Run `/dowser` in the repository you want to scan. `/dowser area: src/checkout` scans one folder; `/dowser goal: <text>` steers the scan towards a goal.

Each scan shows at most 16 proposals, at most 4 per lens, starting with an overview table. Keep, reject, snooze or merge each one. A snoozed proposal comes back when its evidence grows, for example when new tickets ask for it. You can also snooze until a date: it comes back at the first scan on or after that day.

Dowser never writes into your repository. Its memory is in ~/.dowser/projects/<project key>/dowser.db; set DOWSER_HOME to move it.

pages.title: Triage guide for product managers
pages.body:
Switch to guided mode by saying 'switch to guided'. Triage opens with an overview table of every proposal. Say 'full cards' to see each card's summary and description, or 'compact' to go back to the short form.

When you reject a proposal, guided mode asks why in plain words: the evidence does not show this; we already track it or decided it; true, but not where we are going; true, but not worth the effort; right idea, but too big or too small; or something else, in your own words. If a card repeats another one, merge it instead of rejecting it. The reason teaches Dowser what to skip next time.

Ask 'why this one?' about any card to see its evidence. Dowser answers from what it stored and does not scan again.

Snoozing in the Jira inbox can carry a date: the proposal comes back at the first scan on or after that day, or earlier when its evidence grows.

pages.title: Dowser data handling - security review draft
pages.body:
Scope: the Dowser skill on developer laptops and the Dowser for Jira Forge app.

Local store: one SQLite file per project under ~/.dowser, not encrypted at rest; it holds proposal text and the quoted evidence lines.

What leaves the machine: when the Forge app is connected, the skill pushes each proposal's text and its evidence, including the quoted source and doc lines (at most one line each), which the inbox and the Jira issue show. A team can set quotes=omit to push a hash of each line instead of its text; a quoted line repeated in a card's text is replaced by a reference to its file and line.

Dependency auditing runs npm audit, osv-scanner or pip-audit only when they are already installed; Dowser never installs them. The auditors send package names and versions to their advisory services (npm registry, osv.dev, PyPI).

Vulnerability reports: send them to the security contact in the repository's SECURITY.md. Jira and Confluence text a scan fetched is dropped when the scan finishes; an interrupted scan's text is dropped by the first scan that starts more than a day later.

pages.title: Dowser for Jira - operations runbook
pages.body:
Local development without a Jira site: `npm run local:forge` starts the real core on node:sqlite, then `npm run local:ui` serves the Custom UI against it.

Gates before a deploy: `npm run forge:typecheck`, `npm run forge:test`, `npm run forge:check-shared`, then `npm run forge:build-ui`, and for a changed screen a render of it in the fixture UI (`npm --prefix forge/static/app run dev:fixture`), exercising what changed.

The shared modules in forge/src/shared are copies of the skill's model and fingerprint modules; after editing either, run `npm --prefix forge run sync-shared`.

goals.title: Beta teams act on what Dowser proposes
goals.body: Product managers in the closed beta triage a scan in under 10 minutes and accept at least 40% of what they keep. Measured from the Forge inbox verdicts per team, monthly, through Q1 2027.

goals.title: Codegeist 2026: a judge sees the whole loop in 15 minutes
goals.body: Install, first scan, pre-triage, push to the inbox, a verdict and its effect on the next scan, on a fresh machine in 15 minutes from the README alone.

goals.title: CRA-ready open-source release
goals.body: Before the public release: a published vulnerability disclosure contact, an SBOM with each release, signed release artifacts and documented support periods.

opportunity.notes: The beta's outcome is G-1: PMs triage fast and act on what they keep.

docs/project-documentation.md (the original Codegeist plan, kept as history)
